chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about al-'Inah, and I said, 'Indeed, most of our merchants today give al-'Inah, so let me relate to you how it is done.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Go ahead.' I said: 'A haggling man comes to us wanting money, so he haggles with us, and we have no goods. He says, "I will profit you ten, eleven," and I say, "And I, ten, eleven." So we do not cease bargaining until we agree upon a matter.'

When we finish, I say to him, 'Which goods do you prefer that I buy for you?' He says, 'Silk, because we do not find anything less wasteful than it.' So I go, having made a verbal agreement without a formal sale. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that if you wish, you do not give it, and if he wishes, he does not take from you?' I said, 'Yes.'

He (the narrator) said: 'So I go and buy that silk for him, and I bargain to the best of my ability. Then I bring it to my house and sell it to him. Sometimes I add a little to him over the verbal agreement, sometimes I give it to him as agreed, and sometimes we struggle and nothing happens. When he buys from me, he does not find anyone more expensive with it than the one from whom I bought it, so he sells it to him. Then he comes, takes the dirhams, and hands them to him; and sometimes he comes to assign it to me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You do not hand them over except to the owner of the silk.'

I said: 'And sometimes the sale does not agree between me and him, and I seek from him, and he accepts it from me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not that if he wishes, he does not do it, and if you wish, you do not return it?' I said, 'Yes. If he were to die, it would be from my wealth.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with this. When you do not exceed this, there is no problem with it.'

key_terms.الْعِينَة: Buy-back sale (a sale with a repurchase agreement, often used for cash liquidity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on al-'Inah in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the classical 'Inah' mechanism where a merchant sells goods on credit to a cash-needy party, who then immediately resells them for cash to the original seller, effectively creating a loan with interest. Imam al-Rida (AS) validates this practice as permissible (Ja'iz) based on the principle of 'Ikhtiyar' (optionality), noting that since the final sale is not pre-committed and either party can withdraw, it avoids the strict prohibition of Riba in fixed contracts. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the form of the transaction and its substantive economic reality, allowing for liquidity solutions in trade.
